about: Viña Zorzal is run by the Sanz brothers, Xabi, Iñaki and Mikel, in Corella in southern Navarra, where their father Antonio began making his own wines in 1989. The brothers founded Viña Zorzal in 2007 to rescue Navarra’s overlooked native grapes, and it was their work with Graciano that first caught the attention of major critics. Cuatro del Cuatro is their tribute to Antonio, made from the variety that put the winery on the map.

The grapes come from a single plot of roughly forty-year-old, organically farmed Graciano in Ombatillo, on the Corella side of the estate, where the land is flatter and calcareous clay soils hold a more Mediterranean warmth. Fermentation starts spontaneously with native yeasts in 500-litre French oak barrels, and the wine then completes malolactic fermentation and ages twelve months in two-year-old 300-litre barrels. As with all Zorzal wines, it is not fined or filtered and sees only a moderate dose of sulphur.

Graciano is a late-ripening, deeply coloured grape usually used as a small seasoning in Rioja blends; bottled alone it is rare, prized for perfume and lively acidity. The winery calls this the highest expression of Graciano they have found in the region. Production is small, around 3,600 bottles in recent vintages, and critics have described the wine as perfumed, floral and true to its variety.
facts: Single plot in Ombatillo, Corella; vines about 40 years old
Spontaneous fermentation in 500 L French oak barrels
